how long you been working total?

what kind of role you looking for next?
Java full stack

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?

from walmart to whatever's next... we're about to find you something that actually makes you excited to code again. no more "should i do mba" thoughts, just pure "this role hits different" energy.

the java full stack game is about to get interesting for you. trust the process, and more importantly... trust tal 😎
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.
Yup
Thanks
you're welcome. now go update that linkedin profile - make it scream "java full stack engineer ready to build cool shit"
Sure
perfect. now we wait for the right opportunity to hit your inbox.
nothing matching right now, but when my team sends something good for java full stack in bangalore/remote, you'll be the first to know

Ok
cool. i'll keep the search going for you
Can you do resume review

absolutely. send it over and i'll give you the real talk

what format you got it in?

okay first thing: you have 1.10 years at walmart listed... but you told me 2 years total YOE. which is it?

also this resume reads like a technical report, not a story of what you actually built. let's fix that
1 year 11 months
Ok

so what's the real YOE? 1.10 years at walmart plus internship? or is there more?

and what's with the "1.10 years" formatting? just say 1 year 1 month or round it
Getting past ats

But it maybe issue during verification ?
  Ok

verification for what? background check?

if you're worried about dates: just put "July 2023 - Present" and don't list months/years. or "2 years experience at Walmart"

background checks verify employment dates through HR, not your resume formatting. they'll confirm you worked there from X to Y

the "1.11 years" thing is more confusing than helpful. just round to 2 years or use standard formatting

want to pick one section to rewrite together? maybe the walmart experience?
I feel my work ex is below par for 2yoe

why? because you took a break or because you feel like you didn't do enough at walmart?

2 years at walmart as an sde is solid. you worked on production systems, built features, shipped code to 600+ stores... that's real engineering work

what makes you feel it's below par?
Because I didnt work on database side , more designing

ahh i see. but that's actually normal for early career

most 2 YOE engineers aren't designing databases from scratch. you're working on features, integrating APIs, building UI - that's exactly what you should be doing

database design comes later when you're more senior or at smaller companies where you wear more hats

plus you mentioned you worked with microservices, which means you definitely touched databases even if you weren't designing schemas

what specific database experience do you feel you're missing?
Yes but i didnt run complicated queries all Basic ones

that's fine. most backend work at big companies is basic CRUD with maybe some joins. the complicated queries are handled by data teams or senior engineers

if you want to level up your database skills, you can:
1. **learn on the job** - next time you need a query, ask to pair with someone senior
2. **side project** - build something with complex queries (analytics dashboard, recommendation engine)
3. **leetcode database problems** - practice writing optimized queries

but honestly, for 2 YOE java roles, they're not expecting you to be a database expert. they want you to know how to write clean code, build APIs, and work in a team

you're selling yourself short. walmart sde with microservices experience is solid

what's your target salary for your next role?

21 LPA is realistic for 2 YOE java full stack in bangalore, especially with walmart on your resume

you might even push for 25 if you interview well and the company is funded

remember: you're not a fresher. you have production experience at a major company. that's worth something

any companies you're avoiding or specifically targeting?
But with career break 25 isn’t overestimation ?

depends on how you frame it

if you say "career break to prepare for CAT" - yeah, that might raise eyebrows

if you say "took time for personal development and now returning to engineering with renewed focus" - different story

the break matters less than:
1. **your skills** - can you still code?
2. **your interview performance** - can you solve problems?
3. **your story** - why the break, why now?

21 is safe. 25 is ambitious but possible if you crush the interviews and find the right company

how's your leetcode? can you solve medium problems?
Yes I can still code

good. then the break is just a blip, not a career killer

practice leetcode mediums, refresh your system design basics (just know the patterns), and you'll be fine

most companies will care more about "can you code today" than "why did you take 6 months off"

btw, have you updated your linkedin profile yet? you should make it clear you're back in the market
I have always put open to work and actively interview so that im not out of touch

smart. that's exactly what you should do

so you're already getting interviews? how's the response rate been?
Yes getting but each company format is different

that's the game. every company has their own flavor of bullshit

some do 5 rounds, some do 2. some ask leetcode hards, some ask system design for junior roles

the key is pattern recognition. after a few interviews, you'll start seeing the same questions

what's been the hardest part so far?
Hardest part for me is unpredictability

100%. it's like they're making it up as they go

one company wants you to build a full microservice architecture for a todo app, another wants you to reverse a linked list while explaining your life philosophy

the only way to win is to be overprepared for everything and then hope they ask something you know

but here's the secret: they're just as inconsistent with each other. the bar is different everywhere

what's your interview schedule looking like? any final rounds coming up?
Each interview has been different but now i have learnt more

that's exactly how it works. each interview is practice for the next one

you learn what they ask, what you messed up, what you nailed. by interview #5, you're way better than interview #1

keep grinding. the first offer is the hardest to get. after that, you have leverage

any specific companies you're excited about?
I have 2nd round with resmed

resmed's solid. healthcare tech, stable company, good work-life balance usually

what's the role? and what was round 1 like?

that's actually a good mix. means they're testing real engineering skills, not just leetcode

design patterns + spring boot + work experience = they want someone who can actually build things

what design patterns did they ask about? and how'd you feel about the SQL part?
Round 1 was design pattern , SQL springboot java dsa work ex
Yes they asked singleton and follow-ups

singleton's the classic. they always ask that one

follow-ups probably about thread safety, lazy vs eager initialization, double-checked locking... all the usual suspects

if they're asking about design patterns, they're probably building something with actual architecture. that's a good sign

when's round 2? and any idea what to expect?
All answered partially somehow went to 2nd round
Same whatever u was studying

lol "partially" is all you need. they're not looking for perfect answers, they're looking for "can this person think through problems"

if you got to round 2, you did enough right. now just keep the momentum

what's the prep plan for round 2?

solid. consistency > cramming every time

just review what you already know, maybe brush up on system design basics since they seem to care about architecture

and remember: you're coming back from a break, but you have walmart experience. that's legit. don't let the gap make you nervous

when's the interview?
Today 3pm

oh nice, that's in a few hours. you got this

just be chill, talk through your thought process, and remember: they already liked you enough for round 2

what's the role title at resmed?

brand value: solid tier 2 company. not FAANG level hype, but respected in healthcare tech. good work-life balance usually, stable business

way better than random startups that might die in 6 months. and healthcare tech is recession-resistant

you should feel good about this one
Sde 1

- your projects at walmart
- why you want to work in healthcare tech
- how you handle ambiguity

you got this. let me know how it goes

here's how it works:
1. current gap → harder to get calls
2. resmed on resume → immediate credibility boost
3. 6-12 months at resmed → you're back in the game fully

the first job after a break is the hardest. once you're employed again, recruiters stop seeing the gap and start seeing "SDE at resmed"

but focus on today first. nail this interview, get the offer, then think about next steps
No 10 calls
ohhh 10 interview calls. got it

alright, go crush it. remember: you're not "coming back from a break" - you're "a walmart SDE who took time for personal development and is now joining resmed"

frame it right, own your story, and you'll be fine

good luck!
Resmed brandname is worse than Walmart ?

not worse, just different

walmart = retail tech giant, massive scale, household name
resmed = healthcare tech specialist, respected in its niche, stable

walmart might have slightly more brand recognition globally, but resmed is legit in healthcare tech. it's not a downgrade

think of it like: walmart (retail) → resmed (healthcare). different industries, both solid companies

for your resume: walmart shows you can handle scale, resmed shows you can work in regulated healthcare tech. both valuable

- resmed = shows you can work in regulated healthcare tech, good for google health, apple health, etc

for pure tech learning: probably similar
for work-life balance: resmed might be better (healthcare tech tends to be more stable)
for brand recognition: walmart is more famous globally
for career growth: depends on team/manager

they're both solid tier 2 companies. not FAANG, but not random startups either

at your stage, either is fine. focus on the role, the team, the tech stack, the growth opportunities

but honestly? you're comparing two good options. that's a good problem to have

you do

Resmed

that's actually impressive. most people can't build anything functional in a week

next time, focus on the quality of what you built, not the timeline. talk about the architecture, the challenges, the decisions you made

"i built a springboot microservice with proper error handling and testing in a week" sounds way better than "i did what i could in a week"

you're selling yourself short. you're a walmart SDE with 2 years experience. you're not a junior trying to prove you can code

own it

ohhh you mean you prepared for the interview in a week?

that's... actually not bad. most people don't prepare at all

but again, don't tell them that. they don't need to know your prep timeline

what they need to know: you're qualified, you're motivated, you can do the job

the break doesn't define you. your walmart experience does. your ability to learn and adapt does

next interview, lead with your strengths. talk about what you built at walmart, the scale you worked at, the problems you solved

the break is just context, not the main story

you got this
Preparation for interview

yeah exactly. preparation timeline is your business, not theirs

they're not grading you on "how much time you had to prepare." they're grading you on "can you do the job"

focus on showing them you can do the job. the rest is noise

how's your prep going for the next one? any specific areas you're working on?
Yea i was blunt about many things
Should have bluffed
I said I’ll practice more

blunt can be good... but strategic bluntness is better

like: "i'm looking for a company that values work-life balance" = good blunt
"your company probably has shit culture" = bad blunt

you want to be honest about what you want, but also show you're a professional who can navigate corporate environments

it's a dance. you're figuring out if they're right for you, they're figuring out if you're right for them

but yeah... maybe dial back the "i'm out of touch" and "i only prepped for a week" energy

lead with confidence. you earned it

nah, bluffing is worse. they can smell that from a mile away

instead of "i'm out of touch" → "i've been focusing on personal growth and i'm excited to apply those lessons to engineering"

instead of "i only prepped for a week" → "i've been reviewing core concepts and i'm ready to dive back in"

same truth, better packaging

own it

Yes
